result.markdown: --- title: "Testing for Absence and Equivalence" subtitle: "Course 3 (TAE) · how to support a prediction of \"no effect\"" --- A hands-on course that builds on *Linear Models in R*. Many hypotheses in behavioural research predict the *absence* of an effect, yet a non-significant result is often misread as evidence for it. The course teaches two ways to test such predictions properly: frequentist **equivalence tests** and **Bayesian** alternatives. ## Topics - **Why *p* > .05 is not evidence for "no effect":** absence of evidence vs. evidence of absence. - **The smallest effect size of interest (SESOI):** how to justify which effects are too small to matter. - **Equivalence tests (TOST):** how to test predictions of "no effect" with classical significance tests, based on a justified SESOI (R package TOSTER). - **Bayes factors:** quantifying the evidence for the null relative to the alternative (R package BayesFactor). - **Bayesian estimation with a region of practical equivalence (ROPE):** deciding on the basis of the posterior distribution (R packages brms and bayestestR). - **Comparing the approaches:** when they agree, when they differ, and the role of priors. **Outcome:** each participant plans how to test a "no effect" prediction in their own project, including a sample-size justification. ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [*p*-value](../glossary.qmd#p-value), [SESOI (smallest effect size of interest)](../glossary.qmd#sesoi), [Equivalence test (TOST)](../glossary.qmd#equivalence-test), [Bayes factor](../glossary.qmd#bayes-factor), [ROPE (region of practical equivalence)](../glossary.qmd#rope), [Prior, posterior](../glossary.qmd#prior) ::: ## Simulate first: three answers to the same data There is **no difference** between the two groups in these data. The classic *t*-test is non-significant, but that alone says nothing about whether the effect is absent. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(13) n <- 100 a <- rnorm(n); b <- rnorm(n) # true difference = 0 sesoi <- 0.4 # smallest effect of interest (in SD units) # 1. Classic t-test: non-significant, but not evidence for "no effect" t.test(a, b, var.equal = TRUE)$p.value ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> [1] 0.5200304 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # 2. Equivalence test (TOST): is the difference within [-SESOI, +SESOI]? p_lower <- t.test(a, b, mu = -sesoi, alternative = "greater", var.equal = TRUE)$p.value p_upper <- t.test(a, b, mu = sesoi, alternative = "less", var.equal = TRUE)$p.value max(p_lower, p_upper) # < .05 -> effect is statistically equivalent to zero ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> [1] 0.01766867 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # 3. Bayes factor for H0 over H1 (BIC approximation; Wagenmakers, 2007) d <- data.frame(y = c(a, b), group = rep(c("a", "b"), each = n)) m0 <- lm(y ~ 1, data = d) m1 <- lm(y ~ group, data = d) exp((BIC(m1) - BIC(m0)) / 2) # BF01 > 1 favours "no difference" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> [1] 11.46872 ``` ::: ::: In the course, the BIC approximation is replaced by Bayes factors with explicit priors (BayesFactor) and by posterior estimation with a ROPE (brms, bayestestR). ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R scripts coming soon ::: ## Reading and tools - Lakens, D., Scheel, A. M., & Isager, P. M. (2018). Equivalence testing for psychological research: A tutorial. *Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1*(2), 259–269. - Lakens, D., McLatchie, N., Isager, P. M., Scheel, A. M., & Dienes, Z. (2020). Improving inferences about null effects with Bayes factors and equivalence tests. *The Journals of Gerontology: Series B, 75*(1), 45–57. - Dienes, Z. (2014). Using Bayes to get the most out of non-significant results. *Frontiers in Psychology, 5*, 781. - Kruschke, J. K. (2018). Rejecting or accepting parameter values in Bayesian estimation. *Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1*(2), 270–280. - Wagenmakers, E.-J. (2007). A practical solution to the pervasive problems of *p* values. *Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 14*(5), 779–804. - Lakens, D. *Improving your statistical inferences.* - R packages: [TOSTER](https://cran.r-project.org/package=TOSTER), [BayesFactor](https://cran.r-project.org/package=BayesFactor), [brms](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/), [bayestestR](https://easystats.github.io/bayestestR/)
